item.title: Apprenticeship in the Canton of Zurich: a practical guide
item.description: How to find an internship, understand the apprenticeship contract, salaries and professional maturity in the Canton of Zurich.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Swiss apprenticeship: integrated dual system (school + company), typical duration 3-4 years - Canton Zurich: one of the main training hubs with a consistent offer of internships - Mandatory written contract with specific rights: increasing salary per year, 5 weeks under-20 holidays - Professional maturity: certification parallel to the apprenticeship that accesses the SUPs
## Key facts - **What**: Dual vocational training system (company + vocational school) with binding contract - Where: Canton Zurich (applicable in all cantons according to uniform federal law) - When: Duration 3-4 years, starting at 15-16 years post-secondary - Who: Post-compulsory young people; registered training companies; cantonal vocational schools - Rights: Increasing salary per year, legal protection CO art. 344 ff., AVS/AI contributions, 5 weeks under-20 holidays
Apprenticeship in Switzerland is the most common training path for young people after middle school. In the Canton of Zurich, the system works according to the federal dual model: each apprentice alternates days at the training company with days of vocational school, acquiring both practical and theoretical skills. The standard duration is 3-4 years, depending on the business address.
Throughout the course, a written apprenticeship contract governs rights and duties. The company undertakes to train according to federal requirements and sectoral standards; ### Finding an internship in the Canton of Zurich
The offer of traineeships in the Canton of Zurich is published on federal and cantonal platforms managed by professional associations. The main resources are the national brokerage portals (YOUSTY, LENA and similar), where each company registered as a trainer publishes annually the available positions by sector.
The Cantonal Vocational Guidance Office of the Canton of Zurich collects information on places, carries out individual counselling for young people and provides data on training companies active in the territory. In addition, trade unions and professional associations for specific sectors (construction, electronics, commerce, hospitality, agriculture) publish dedicated offers.
The research should begin 12-18 months before the end of middle school. Young people spontaneously send applications to training companies, attaching school report card, motivational letter, personal curriculum. Selection interviews and short aptitude tests at the company often follow.
### The apprenticeship contract: rights and obligations
The binding contract stipulated between apprentice (and parents if minor), training company and competent cantonal office contains elements standardized by federal law:
- ** Total duration ** of the apprenticeship (example: 3 years, 4 years) - Professional sector and Federal Certificate of Competence number (AFC — Certificate of Vocational Training) - Monthly salary
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### The professional maturity: parallel certification to the apprenticeship
An even more attractive path is the **professional maturity** (PM), a federal certification that can be obtained parallel to the apprenticeship without extending the overall duration of the training. The PM allows direct access to professional universities (PU — Fachhochschulen) without requiring an additional year of complementary training.
In the Canton of Zurich, vocational schools offer professional maturity modules integrated into the apprenticeship curriculum, typically with 1-2 additional lessons per week. Access to the PM depends on school performance during the apprenticeship: educational institutions evaluate aptitudes in mathematics, languages, and technical subjects. The consequence of the PM is a federal certificate that certifies both professional skills and academic preparation.
### Step-by-step procedure to start
Phase 1 — Orientation and research (months 10-12 of middle school)
Consult the cantonal orientation office of the Canton of Zurich, participate in professional fairs and school orientation days, discuss with parents and teachers, identify 5-10 realistic sectors of interest based on personal aptitudes and local market.
Phase 2 — Active application (months 18-6 before the end of middle school)
Regularly visit federal portals of internship offers (YOUSTY, LENA, professional association websites), write a concise CV and personalized motivational letter, contact training companies directly in the chosen sector, participate in informative meetings and company open days, prepare for aptitude tests and selection interviews.
Phase 3 — Negotiation and contract signing (months 3 before the start of the apprenticeship)
Receive and evaluate the binding internship offer, sign the contract (parents will sign if underage), deposit the contract with the competent cantonal office, receive the official administrative confirmation and the summons for the first day of work.
Phase 4 — Start of the apprenticeship
The first day of work marks the beginning of the trial period (3 months). During this period, both the apprentice and the company can terminate without notice and without special justification. At the end of the trial period, the contract becomes fully binding for both parties until the completion of the path.
### Practical tools to deepen and compare opportunities
To evaluate your estimated salary as an apprentice in the Canton of Zurich and compare the evolution of remuneration in different years, use the salary calculator. A tool that estimates the gross and net amount based on the professional sector and canton of work.
Additionally, consult the [job and apprenticeship offers](nav:jobs) regularly published: many companies release new internship positions in predictable cycles during the school year. The investment in professional training pays off concretely: apprentices who complete the path access the job market with federal certificates recognized throughout Switzerland, defined career prospects in the specific profession, and access to further continuing education (specialization courses, professional maturity, higher education).

item.title: Novartis cuts 130 jobs in Basel
item.description: Novartis announces the cut of up to 130 jobs in Basel by the end of 2027. Reason: transfer of activities to Novartis Campus and expiration of contracts.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Novartis to cut up to 130 jobs by the end of 2027 in Basel - Reason: expiration of Kleinbasel contracts, transfer to Novartis Campus - Since 2018: nearly 3,000 layoffs by Novartis in Switzerland
## Key facts - **What**: Job cuts in low-volume biologics production - When: By the end of 2027 - Where: Basel, Kleinbasel district - Who: Novartis (pharmaceutical group) - Number: Up to 130 jobs
Novartis announces the cut of up to 130 jobs at its Basel site. The decision was communicated on Wednesday by the Swiss pharmaceutical group and will take effect by the end of 2027. Due to the expiration of lease contracts in the Kleinbasel district, the production of low-volume biologics will be abandoned at the current site. This is part of a broader production reorganization strategy that Novartis has been pursuing for years.
The biological production activities will not completely disappear from Basel: they will be transferred to other production sites worldwide. Meanwhile, several divisions will transfer their operations from the Kleinbasel district to the Novartis Campus, located on the other side of the Rhine. Among the activities involved are laboratories for biological cell banks, analytical testing procedures, and offices dedicated to technical development.
This transfer represents the continuation of previously announced plans to build a new center specializing in the technical development of biologics at the campus. This center will integrate with the existing biologics research center within the structure.
### Consultation and social plan All planned changes are subject to the information and consultation process. Novartis is committed to supporting the affected employees with a series of offers, including a long-term social plan. This support will be discussed and negotiated during the consultation phase with worker representatives.
The consultation process is a critical moment for the affected employees: it allows them to negotiate the terms of the restructuring and to explore alternative options to layoffs. During this phase, unions will play a crucial role in protecting workers' interests. ### A worrying trend for Swiss employment
The announcement by Novartis comes nine months after the previous major job cut in Stein, in Aargau. Since 2018, the group has eliminated nearly 3,000 jobs in Switzerland. This figure reflects a corporate restructuring strategy that has been ongoing for years and significantly impacts the Swiss job market.
The cuts since 2018 represent a total of nearly 3,000 lost jobs. The Swiss pharmaceutical sector is directly affected by the loss of qualified employment in companies of the caliber of Novartis. Restructuring in large companies indirectly influences the local economy and cantonal social services.
### The position of the unions
The union Unia has expressed "alarm at the continued dismantling of production jobs in Switzerland." The union's request is clear: Novartis should refrain from layoffs and ensure the continuation of employment for workers at another site in northwestern Switzerland, rather than transferring production abroad.
This position highlights the issue of relocation: the transfer of production to other countries raises doubts about the long-term effects on Switzerland's productive capacity. For workers directly affected, negotiation during the consultation phase will be crucial to obtain the maximum possible support. Workers should also verify how any salary changes will impact Swiss wages and salaries through the online calculator available.

The information and consultation process initiated by Novartis is mandatory and represents the crucial moment in which workers and unions can negotiate the terms of the restructuring. During this phase, employee representatives have the right to discuss with the company the aspects of the restructuring, including possible alternatives to layoffs.
The long-term social plan announced by Novartis must be presented and negotiated during this consultation phase. It is in this context that workers will be able to understand in detail what forms of support will be made available to facilitate the transition. The right to consultation is a fundamental guarantee for workers in the context of restructurings of this magnitude.
### Role of unions in negotiations
The union Unia represents an essential point of reference for Novartis workers affected by the restructuring. Unia provides free advice to its members to negotiate the conditions of the transfer and the social plan. Those who are not members of a union can still request the support of company union delegates during the scheduled consultation meetings.
Union advice is completely free, and representatives can help workers understand their rights, negotiate the best possible conditions, and plan the transition to new employment. Coordinated action during the consultation phase increases the bargaining power of employees and improves the prospects of a favorable occupational transition.
### Job search and available resources
Workers affected by the restructuring will need to plan their job search. In Switzerland, there are [job openings in the national job market](nav:jobs) that can facilitate the transition to a new position. It is advisable for workers to start this search promptly, also taking advantage of the resources and contacts offered by Novartis' social plan.
To verify the impact of the occupational transition on the tax return and taxable income, workers can consult the [guide to the Swiss tax return](nav:tax-return). Maintaining close contact with unions throughout the consultation and negotiation phase remains crucial to protect their interests.

item.title: PA 2030+: more freedom for Swiss farmers
item.description: The Federal Council launches consultation on PA30+: management autonomy, less bureaucracy, digitalisation and CHF 13.8 billion of investment for agriculture 2030-2033.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal Council launches PA30+ consultation until December 8 - More management autonomy for farmers, less bureaucracy - Spending 2030-2033: 13.8 billion CHF (-123 million vs 2026-2029)
## Key facts - **What**: Agricultural Policy 2030+ with 4 areas of intervention - When: Consultation until December 8; in force 2030-2033 - Where: Switzerland (all cantons) - Who: Federal Council, farmers, traders, consumers - Amount: 13.8 billion CHF for 2030-2033
The Federal Council today announced the Agricultural Policy 2030+ (PA30+), a new regulatory framework for the Swiss agricultural sector aimed at increasing national food security by expanding farmers' operational leeway. The consultation remains open until December 8.
"The actors in the agri-food chain and consumers are called upon to take on greater responsibilities to ensure an ecologically, economically, and socially sustainable food system," the executive explained in a statement. Federal President Guy Parmelin outlined the details during a press conference.
### The four strategic areas of PA30+
The PA30+ is structured around four strategic areas. The first concerns the expansion of farmers' operational leeway and the reduction of administrative burden through digitalization. Currently, direct payments to farmers are closely linked to compliance with certain prescriptions. With PA30+, these payments will increasingly be linked to the actual results achieved, offering greater management freedom.
To support this transition, the Federal Council intends to substantially raise the entry thresholds for direct payments in the lowland and hilly zones, as well as for structural improvements in the lowland zone. "In this way, we aim to reduce costs and ask farmers to find synergies among themselves," Parmelin explained.
The second area concerns the proper functioning of markets. The executive intends to strengthen market observation and extend solidarity measures to help agricultural businesses value their products and strengthen their position in the domestic market. Additional specific support is also planned for the dairy sector and for crops directly intended for human consumption, with the aim of improving farmers' economic situation.
The third area addresses crop protection. Measures are planned to promote beneficial insects and organisms in biological control, support the development of sustainable technologies, and strengthen training and advice for farmers. In this way, agricultural businesses will receive greater support in adapting to climate change.
The last area concerns the involvement of retail trade and consumers. The government intends to promote sustainability throughout the value chain through agreements on objectives with traders and greater awareness among citizens towards Swiss products. This approach aims to positively influence the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) through a more transparent supply chain. ### How agricultural payments are changing
The Federal Council intends to submit to Parliament the spending limits for agriculture for the period 2030-2033, for a total of 13.8 billion francs. This amount represents a reduction of 123 million francs compared to the previous period (2026-2029), but still an increase of 80 million compared to what would be available if the 2030 financial plan were maintained at nominal values.
The reduction compared to the previous three-year period reflects the efficiency objective of PA30+: through the reduction of administrative burden and the strengthening of digitalization, the system aims to achieve the same support for the sector with slightly lower costs. However, compared to a scenario of simple continuity, PA30+ represents an additional investment of 80 million.
One of the most significant changes concerns the shift from payments linked to compliance with prescriptions to payments linked to results. This system offers farmers greater flexibility in choosing the operational methods to achieve sustainability, environmental protection, and food safety goals.
The increase in entry thresholds for direct payments, particularly in the plains and hills, represents a structural incentive to promote aggregations and synergies between companies. Smaller companies could associate to meet the required thresholds, allowing them to access direct payments and structural improvements. This mechanism reduces the fragmentation of the sector and promotes economies of scale.
### The central role of the Swiss consumer
PA30+ recognizes that the end consumer plays a crucial role in supporting the sustainable food system. Through agreements on objectives with traders and awareness of Swiss products, it is intended to create a positive dynamic that connects agricultural supply with conscious consumer demand.
This shift from the supply side to a multi-stakeholder approach (farmers, traders, consumers, institutions) represents a paradigm shift in how Switzerland manages food security. It is no longer just about subsidizing production, but about building an ecosystem where all actors share responsibilities and benefits.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Participation in the consultation
The consultation on PA30+ remains open until December 8. This period is intended to collect feedback from farmers, industry associations, traders, environmental organizations, and interested citizens.
Those wishing to contribute can submit observations and proposals directly to the Federal Council. The specific methods of participation (format of observations, transmission addresses, possible regional information meetings) must be verified on the official website of the Swiss government or with the cantonal agricultural administrations, which often facilitate the dialogue between their farmers and the federal consultation.
### Practical implications for the agricultural sector
For farmers, PA30+ represents a concrete opportunity to reduce bureaucracy. The digitization of the application and monitoring processes for direct payments should significantly simplify administrative management, freeing up time and resources for production activities. At the same time, the increase in entry thresholds represents a stimulus to rethink the organizational structure: associations between small farms, cooperatives, or sharing of infrastructure could offer new [employment opportunities](nav:jobs) and synergies in the sector.
For traders, the agreements on objectives with the Federal Council represent a shared framework for promoting Swiss agricultural products. This creates opportunities for differentiation and marketing linked to sustainability, strengthening the connection between conscious consumers and local quality supply.
### Next steps and time horizon
The presentation to Parliament of the spending limits will take place after the conclusion of the consultation, probably in 2027. Parliamentary approval will be necessary before PA30+ can fully enter into force for the period 2030-2033.
In the meantime, farmers and sector operators should stay informed about the developments of the consultation. Contacting the cantonal professional agricultural associations and following the official channels of the Federal Council allows you to keep up with the news.
For those who need information on the current direct payments to farmers, on the structure of federal subsidies, and on the calculation of the contributions that will benefit from the new thresholds, it is advisable to consult the dedicated federal support and information services.

item.title: Switzerland less attractive to multinationals: McKinsey alarm
item.description: 70% of CEOs warn that Switzerland is losing competitiveness. Criticisms of lengthy procedures, OECD tax and poor infrastructure threaten foreign investment.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 70% of CEOs believe Switzerland is losing international appeal - Main criticisms: lengthy procedures (70%), OECD minimum tax (65%), inadequate infrastructure (60%) - Multinationals generate 42% of Swiss GDP, despite being 6% of businesses
## Key facts - **What**: Study on Switzerland's loss of appeal for multinationals - When: Published today - Who: McKinsey and Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce - Amount: 70% CEOs convinced of the loss; 42% GDP from multinationals; 6% multinational businesses - Criticisms: Procedures (+70%), OECD tax (+65%), infrastructure (+60%)
Seven out of ten business leaders are convinced that the Swiss economic hub is losing its advantages compared to international competition. The alarm was sounded by a study published by the consulting firm McKinsey and the Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce. According to the report, the Confederation remains the leading European hub for research and development but attracts fewer global company headquarters and fewer international executives than in the past. 70% of the CEOs surveyed believe that Switzerland is taking steps backward regarding its international appeal.
### Main criticisms Three specific areas concentrate managerial complaints. The lengthening of approval procedures for investment projects and work permits for foreign talent was reported by 70% of respondents. The introduction of the OECD minimum tax concerns 65%, while infrastructure bottlenecks are highlighted by 60%.
According to the managers interviewed, geopolitical tensions, new trade barriers, uncertainty in relations with the European Union, and the strength of the franc also weigh on perception.
### The crucial role of multinationals Multinationals play an essential role in the Swiss economy. Although they represent only 6% of businesses in Switzerland, they generate 42% of Swiss GDP and are the source of three-quarters of nominal economic growth since 2014. Losing competitiveness in this segment would have significant repercussions on employment, territorial development, and overall country growth. ## What does this loss mean for those working in Switzerland?
### Implications for economic growth
The contraction of attractiveness mentioned by McKinsey is not purely a statistical phenomenon. Since 2014, multinational companies have generated three-quarters of Switzerland's nominal economic growth. If this positive dynamic were to reverse, overall investments, salary opportunities, and direct and indirect jobs would slow down. This is not a remote risk: the report explicitly states that the Confederation is already attracting fewer global company headquarters and fewer international executives than in the past.
### The three knots to untie
Three specific factors require urgent intervention, according to the opinion of CEOs. Approval procedures for investments and work permits have become slower—a critical issue highlighted by 70% of respondents. The imposition of the OECD minimum tax was perceived as a competitive burden by 65% of managers. And infrastructure, from energy to transportation, shows structural bottlenecks (noted by 60%).
[Discover how to monitor job opportunities in Switzerland](nav:jobs).
### Balance between regulation and competitiveness
A critical point of the McKinsey report: a strong economic hub is not built through wild deregulation. It requires "efficient, proportionate, and predictable framework conditions that allow for innovation, investment, and growth." This means that Switzerland does not have to choose between regulatory rigor and attractiveness but must find a balance that allows international businesses to operate with legal certainty and administrative speed.
### The context of geopolitical pressure
In addition to the structural issues of regulation and taxation, McKinsey and the Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce highlight the role of global geopolitical tensions, new trade barriers, and uncertainty in relations between Switzerland and the European Union. This is compounded by the volatility of the Swiss franc, which affects currency competitiveness for multinational companies operating in euros and dollars. These external factors amplify the damage caused by internal structural weaknesses.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## How to reverse the trend: the five-axis plan
### The pillars of the strategy according to McKinsey
The report identifies five priority areas to preserve the country's attractiveness in the long term, and their implementation will require coordination between the Confederation and the cantons. The first is to ensure access to international talent, accelerating work permits and making the country attractive to foreign professionals. The second is to streamline regulatory procedures, reducing authorization times for projects and investments. The third is to build fiscal predictability, clearly communicating how Switzerland will implement the OECD minimum tax and avoiding tax surprises. The fourth is to invest in infrastructure, especially in mobility, energy, and telecommunications. The fifth is to define a coherent strategic positioning towards the European Union, the United States, and Asia.
### Who decides what: the distribution of responsibilities
The responsibility for reversing the trend is distributed among multiple levels of government. The procedures for granting work permits (category L for short-term, B for residence, C for domicile, G for cross-border commuters) depend on the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) and the cantonal authorities. The implementation of the OECD minimum tax is a federal competence, following international directives. Infrastructure involves both the Confederation and the cantons. Strategic coherence towards the United States, the European Union, and Asia is the responsibility of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs. There is no single "lever" to pull: effective coordination between levels is needed.
### How to follow the progress
Frontaliere Ticino recommends monitoring the next McKinsey reports and observing the data from the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) on new multinational settlements and work permits issued. The Federal Statistical Office (FSO) also publishes data on economic growth and the contribution of multinationals to national GDP. These tools allow evaluating whether federal and cantonal policies are effectively reversing the loss of competitiveness signaled by the study.

item.description: Tobias Walser, an expert in environmental sciences, was appointed delegate of the university assemblies of the Federal Polytechnics of Zurich and Lausanne.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Federal Council appoints Tobias Walser. - He takes office on 1 September 2026. - He succeeds Kristin Becker van Slooten.
## Key facts - **What**: Appointment of Tobias Walser. - When: 1 September 2026. - Where: Council of the ETHs. - Who: Tobias Walser. - Amount: Not specified.
On 2 September 2026, the Federal Council appointed Tobias Walser, an expert in environmental sciences, as the delegate of the university assemblies of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology (ETHs) in Zurich and Lausanne to the Council of the ETHs. Walser, who has been the director of the Department of Health Sciences and Technology at the ETH Zurich since 2022, will take office on 1 September 2026. He succeeds Kristin Becker van Slooten, who held the position from 2004 to 2006 and subsequently from 2017.
Tobias Walser studied environmental sciences at the ETH Zurich, earning his doctorate in 2012 in the field of risk assessment of nanomaterials. For his interdisciplinary work on the spread of nanomaterials, he was awarded the Swiss Aerosol Award in 2012. In his current role as director, he is also involved in strategic initiatives that combine technology, regulation, and practice. He has extensive experience in governance, institutional development, and the coordination of various interest groups in the fields of education and research.
### The Role of Tobias Walser Tobias Walser, with his appointment, assumes a crucial role in the governance of the two largest federal universities in Switzerland. His experience and expertise will be essential in guiding the university assemblies of the ETHs in Zurich and Lausanne, contributing to the definition of national academic strategies and policies. The appointment of Tobias Walser represents a significant step for the Federal Polytechnics of Zurich and Lausanne. His extensive experience in the field of environmental sciences and academic governance will be instrumental in addressing future challenges and promoting innovation and research. Walser succeeds Kristin Becker van Slooten, who held the role from 2004 to 2006 and subsequently from 2017.
### Practical Implications Walser's appointment will have concrete implications for the academic and research community in Switzerland. His experience in governance and institutional development will be crucial to lead the university assemblies of FPs in Zurich and Lausanne. Walser will be responsible for defining academic strategies and policies, helping to promote innovation and research at the national level.

item.title: The more you work, the more you stay: the Ticino laps reform
item.description: The League calls for a reform of the laps with temporary incentives to work to eliminate the “poverty trap” and combat the impact of the LAMal awards.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The Ticino League calls for a reform of the laps with temporary work incentives - Objective: eliminate the "poverty trap" where increasing wages reduces benefits - Model already tested in social assistance: supplement of CHF 300 for those who reach 100% activation
## Key facts - **What**: Motion to reform the Law on Harmonization and Coordination of Social Benefits (laps) - When: Recently presented at the Grand Council - Where: Bellinzona, Ticino - Who: Grand Councillors Stefano Tonini and Alessandro Mazzoleni (and co-signatories) - Amount: Up to CHF 300 per month supplement for 100% job activation
A motion by the Ticino League proposes a profound reform of the laps to strengthen incentives to work and promote the economic autonomy of the beneficiaries. The proposal, presented by the great directors Stefano Tonini and Alessandro Mazzoleni and co-signed by Raffaella Zucchetti, Omar Balli, Sem Genini and Stefano Quadri, starts from a concrete observation: the increase in the cost of living and, above all, in health insurance premiums ([LAMal/KVG](nav:health)) are increasingly eroding the disposable income of Ticino's domestic economies.
The motioners recognise the essential role of cantonal social benefits, but call on the system to give higher priority to work, vocational reintegration and economic autonomy than a lasting dependence on state aid.
### The ### Concrete implications for beneficiaries and migration law
The proposed additional incentive should not constitute a new permanent benefit, but rather a time-limited promotional component. For this reason, the movers request that, to the maximum extent permitted by higher law, it be reserved for Swiss citizens and foreigners holding a residence permit C.
This choice has implications for the group of beneficiaries: the State Council will have to find a legally sustainable solution, taking into account the different situations of EU/EFTA citizens, third-country nationals, and other statuses protected by federal or international law. This is not a purely administrative matter, but one of compliance with Swiss migration law.
### AFI and API: a new legal qualification
A second chapter of the proposal concerns the supplementary allowance (AFI) and the early childhood allowance (API). The signatories request a review of their regulations so that they are configured as social benefits for economic support linked to need and subsidiarity, and when reasonably required, activation towards autonomy, rather than as family promotion measures.
This is a delicate move. Federal case law, particularly the DTF 141 II 401 decision, has qualified AFI and API as family policy instruments, excluding them from constituting social aid under migration law for this very reason. DTF 143 I 1 has also reconstructed the origin and family purposes of the benefits and examined the different access conditions provided for Swiss citizens and foreigners.
For the movers, any new qualification could not be limited to a simple change of name, but would require substantial changes to the purpose, structure, and conditions of the benefits. In other words: if AFI and API were to become social benefits for need-based support (rather than family benefits), the consequences for access rights and activation obligations would be significant.
True family promotion measures — those that go beyond covering an economic need and pursue objectives such as supporting the family, birth rates, and the reconciliation of family and professional life — should instead be regulated separately. On this point, the motion invites a resumption of the debate initiated in 2024 by the "Poker of initiatives to boost birth rates in Ticino" by the Gruppo il Centro + GdC.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### What changes for those receiving social benefits
If the motion is approved by the Grand Council and subsequently implemented by the State Council, LAPS benefit recipients will be able to count on stronger incentives when they increase their work activity. Instead of losing franc for franc the help they received, they will have access to an additional franchise, financial incentives, and reimbursement of expenses directly related to work.
In practice, the choice to move from a 40% job to a 60% job would become concretely advantageous, as the net (salary + incentives - reduction in aid) would be significantly positive.
### How to monitor and act
Those currently receiving social benefits in Ticino should: 1. Check the text of the motion when it is voted on in the Grand Council (normally on the parliamentary transparency portals of Ticino) 2. Contact the AI Office (Integrated Assistance) or the cantonal social service for clarifications on the times and methods of implementation 3. Concretely evaluate whether increasing the degree of employment is convenient, once the details of the incentives are known
Those currently unemployed or underemployed and who may be entitled to LAPS should monitor the evolution of the reform: if it passes, it could become economically sensible to seek more hours of work.
### Understanding the context of LAMal premiums
The motion itself starts from a crucial premise: the premiums of the health insurance (LAMal/KVG) are eroding the available income of Ticino families. This is a relevant national data point: LAMal premiums vary by canton and age class, and the Canton of Ticino provides cantonal subsidies to reduce the burden on low-income beneficiaries.
Consult the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to understand how your gross income is transformed into net after taxes, pension contributions (AVS/AI/IPG, LPP), and, crucially, after the share you will pay for the LAMal premium. Understanding this impact is the first step to understanding whether an increase in employment (and LAPS incentives) is convenient for you.

item.title: Permit L Zurich: validity, renewal and extension
item.description: Permit L: maximum duration of one year, renewable if the contract continues. Transition to permit B and employer constraints in the Canton of Zurich.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Permit L: validity **maximum of 1 year** from issuance - Renewable if the employment contract continues with the same employer - Tied to the employer: job change requires administrative modification - Possible transition to Permit B (renewable residence) after 1–2 years
## Key facts - What: Short-term Permit L for fixed-term employment contract in Switzerland - Duration: Up to 12 months from the date of issuance by the SEM - Where: Managed by the SEM at the federal level; renewals coordinated by the cantons - Who: Non-EU/EFTA citizens and some EU citizens with a fixed-term contract - Tie: Associated with a specific employer named in the permit
The short-term Permit L is the entry document for those wishing to work in Switzerland with a fixed-term contract. It has a maximum validity of one year from issuance and is not automatically renewable: renewal depends on the continuity of the employment relationship and the assessment of the competent cantonal administration.
### What is Permit L Permit L is one of the categories of foreign permits (SEM) managed by the Central Information System on Migration. It differs from permanent permits: Permit B allows renewable residence, Permit C allows stable domicile (normally after 10 years of residence, or 5 years for EU/EFTA citizens).
Regarding access to the Swiss labor market, the holder of Permit L can only work for the employer specified in the initial application — there is a tie to the employer which is one of the differentiating factors compared to those who hold a Permit B. This means that a change of employer requires a modification of the documentation with the canton of residence.
In addition to the permit, every worker in Switzerland must take out [compulsory health insurance (LAMal)](nav:health) within 3 months of arrival. The mandatory contributions to be borne by the employee include AVS/AI/IPG (5.3% of salary) and LAINF/LAA (0.7–1.5% depending on the sector). ### Duration and Expiration of Permit L
The Permit L is valid for **up to 1 year** from the date of issuance. The canton and the SEM do not issue Permit L for different durations: the maximum is set at 12 months. This does not automatically mean that the permit cannot be renewed, but that the initial issuance has an annual validity. At the end, if the employment contract continues and the employer requests an extension (submitting an updated contract), the administration evaluates whether to renew the same Permit L or to transition the worker to Permit B.
The competent canton is normally the one where the worker resides. In the case of the Canton of Zurich, it is the Migration Office of the Zurich Cantonal Police that manages renewals and modifications after the initial issuance by the SEM.
### Scenarios of Extension and Renewal
Scenario 1: Renewal of the Same Permit L
The employer communicates to the canton that the contract continues. If there are no significant changes (same position, same salary, same location), the canton can renew the Permit L for an additional year. This can happen as long as the employer intends to maintain the employment relationship. There is no theoretical maximum limit on subsequent renewals, but each renewal is evaluated individually and lasts up to 1 year.
Scenario 2: Transition to Permit B
After 1–2 years of stable employment with Permit L, the employer and the worker can decide together to request conversion to Permit B (renewable residence). This is a natural step for those who intend to stay in Switzerland for a longer period and is associated with greater administrative stability. Permit B has an initial validity of 5 years and is renewable thereafter.
The transition from L to B is conditioned on: continuity of at least 1–2 years of employment, economic stability of the relationship, and positive evaluation by the cantonal administration.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Renewal procedure and required documents
To renew the L permit upon expiration, the procedure is as follows:
1. **Document collection**: the employer prepares an updated employment contract (or confirmation of the existing contract), salary statement, and certification of contributions [AVS/AI/IPG](nav:pension) (5.3% charged to the employee, 10.6% total with the employer) paid during the first year.
2. Request to the canton: 3–4 weeks before the L permit expires, the employer submits the renewal request to the Migration Office of the Zurich Cantonal Police (often through the canton's online portal).
3. Evaluation: the canton verifies that the contract is still in effect, that there are no defaults in mandatory contributions, and that the worker is compliant with federal, cantonal, and municipal taxes.
4. Issuance: if everything is in order, the canton coordinates the issuance of a new L permit with a maximum validity of 1 year.
⚠️ Attention: If the renewal request is not submitted before the expiration date, the worker loses their legal status to work in Switzerland. Even a few days of delay can result in significant consequences (sanctions for the employer, obligation to pay unpaid contributions, risk of repatriation). It is crucial to coordinate deadlines with the employer and the canton well in advance.
### Constraints related to the employer
One of the main constraints of the L permit is the association with a specific employer. Unlike the B or C permit, the holder of an L permit can only work for the employer named in the permit, cannot change employment without administrative modification with the canton, and cannot engage in self-employment without new federal authorization.
If the worker intends to change employers before the permit expires, they must notify the canton and the SEM. The new employer must submit a new work authorization request (work permit), which is evaluated with priority criteria for Swiss and European workers. If the change of employer coincides with the permit expiration, the procedure becomes even more complex.
For the employer, the constraints are mainly bureaucratic: they must document the employment relationship, pay AVS/AI/IPG contributions, comply with working hour regulations (maximum 45 hours/week for industry, offices, sales; 50 hours for other sectors), ensure a minimum of 4 weeks of annual leave, and notify the canton of any changes in position, salary, or early termination of the contract.
### Next steps and practical tools
For specific requests regarding the L permit in the Canton of Zurich, contact the Migration Office of the Zurich Cantonal Police. For federal issues related to migration, refer to the SEM.
The [salary calculator](nav:calculator) of Frontaliere Ticino helps understand the impact of mandatory contributions (AVS/AI/IPG, LAINF/LAA) and taxes on the gross salary.

item.description: The Swiss franc falls against the euro to a one-year low. The exchange rate reached 0.9435 francs per euro.

## In brief - The Swiss franc falls against the euro, hitting a one-year low. - The exchange rate reached 0,9435 francs per euro. - The interest rate differential between Switzerland and the Eurozone weighs on the Swiss currency. ## Key facts - **What**: The Swiss franc falls against the euro. - When: Not specified. - Where: Switzerland. - Who: Swiss National Bank (SNB), European Central Bank (ECB). - Amount: 0,9435 francs per euro.
The Swiss franc continues to weaken against the euro, a trend that has been noticeable for days. Today, the European currency reached a high of 0,9435 francs, a level not seen since August 2025. Experts attribute this phase of weakness in the Swiss currency primarily to the interest rate differential between Switzerland and the Eurozone.
The currency trend might seem paradoxical in an internationally tense context, but it is mainly explained by the sudden return of the interest rate theme to the forefront, explains John Plassard, the investment strategy manager at the bank Cité Gestion. 'It is not Switzerland (and its safe-haven currency) that suddenly inspires less confidence, but the euro that is regaining an advantage in terms of yield that it had largely lost in recent years.'
The gap between the Swiss National Bank's (SNB) key rate, currently at 0.00%, and the European Central Bank's (ECB) rate, at 2.25%, makes investments in euros more profitable than those in francs. With inflation in the Eurozone reaching 3.3% in August, a more restrictive monetary policy from the ECB is also on the horizon. 'The market already considers a deposit rate of 2.50% as a given, and, above all, it is beginning to wonder how long Frankfurt will have to maintain this stricter line,' comments Plassard.
In the next two weeks, both the ECB and the Federal Reserve will decide on monetary policy. While a rise in the cost of money is certain in the Eurozone, the situation in the United States is not yet entirely clear, although expectations of a rate hike have increased. For its part, the SNB will present its assessment of the situation on September 24: analysts predict that the institution led by Martin Schlegel will opt for the status quo.
### Implications for the Swiss economy
The weakness of the franc against the euro has significant implications for the Swiss economy. A weaker franc makes imports more expensive, which can increase inflation. However, it can also make Swiss exports more competitive in international markets. Investors may be attracted to investments in euros, given their higher profitability compared to francs.
### Future scenarios
With the ECB preparing for a more restrictive monetary policy, it is likely that the interest rate differential between Switzerland and the Eurozone will remain wide. This could keep pressure on the Swiss franc, leading to further fluctuations in the exchange rate. Analysts will be watching the decisions of the SNB and the ECB in the coming weeks for a clearer idea of future currency trends. ## Practical analysis
The weakening of the franc against the euro has concrete implications for Swiss citizens and businesses. For consumers, a weaker franc means that imported products, such as electronics and consumer goods, could become more expensive. On the other hand, holidays in Europe may be cheaper for Swiss tourists.
### Impact on businesses
For Swiss companies, a weaker franc can represent an opportunity to increase exports. However, companies that depend on imports may face higher costs. Firms will need to closely monitor currency fluctuations and adopt strategies to mitigate the associated risks.
### Monetary Policy
The SNB kept the lead rate at 0.00%, while the ECB has a rate of 2.25%. This differential makes investments in euros more attractive than those in francs. With inflation in the Eurozone at 3.3%, the ECB is likely to adopt a tighter monetary policy, further increasing the rate differential.
### Future decisions
In the next two weeks, both the ECB and the Federal Reserve will decide on monetary policy. While an increase in rates is a given in the Eurozone, the situation in the United States is less clear. The SNB will present its assessment on September 24, and analysts expect the institution to opt for the status quo.

Companies that depend on imports or exports should adopt strategies to mitigate the risks associated with currency fluctuations. This may include the use of financial instruments such as forward contracts or currency options to hedge against exchange rate changes.

## In brief - Federal Council opens consultation on PA30+ until December 8 - 13.8 billion CHF allocated for 2030-2033 - 4 areas of intervention on ecology, markets, crops, consumers - Greater autonomy for farmers, responsibility of the supply chain
## Key facts - **What**: Agricultural Policy Reform with 4 areas of intervention - When: Consultation until December 8, implementation from 2030 - Where: All of Switzerland, federal decision - Who: Federal Council, farmers, supply chain actors, consumers - Amount: 13.8 billion CHF for 2030-2033 - Reduction: -123 million vs 2026-2029 - Increase: +80 million vs 2030 financial plan - Focus: Food security, sustainability, animal welfare
The Federal Council has officially opened the consultation on the Agricultural Policy from 2030 (PA30+), with a deadline set for December 8. The reform revolves around a central objective: to expand the margin of maneuver for farmers to strengthen Switzerland's food security. This is a rewrite of the rules that will affect the entire agri-food chain, from producers to consumers.
The Executive emphasizes that it is not just the responsibility of farmers. PA30+ actively involves other actors in the agri-food chain and consumers themselves, who will have to take on greater responsibilities to ensure a sustainable food system from an ecological, economic, and social point of view. This rethinking of competencies represents an important novelty compared to previous policies.
### The four areas of intervention
The reform develops along four strategic axes.
The first area concerns direct payments on ecology and animal welfare. The Federal Council revolutionizes the mechanism of contributions, orienting them towards concrete results rather than strict compliance with regulatory prescriptions. Digitalization plays a crucial role in reducing the administrative burden throughout the chain. A new legal basis will support these changes.
The second area focuses on market functioning. The Executive intends to strengthen market observation and extend solidarity measures. Additional support is planned for the dairy sector and for vegetable crops intended for human consumption—two pillars of Swiss production.
The third area concerns crop protection. Here the focus is on measures that promote beneficial insects and organisms, the use of sustainable technologies, and the strengthening of training and advice to farmers. A relevant aspect concerns the adaptation of farms to climate change, a theme increasingly urgent for the economic viability of crops.
The fourth area involves retail trade and consumers. The Government wants to promote sustainability through agreements on objectives with traders and greater awareness of Swiss products.
### The federal budget: 13.8 billion CHF
The Federal Council has submitted to Parliament the spending limits for agriculture in the period 2030-2033: 13.8 billion francs. The amount is lower by 123 million compared to the period 2026-2029, but higher by 80 million compared to the 2030 financial plan. In other words, the reform involves a compression compared to the current cycle, but still represents an increase compared to the initial forecasts for the decade.
Until December 8, the consultation remains open to public entities, agricultural organizations, consumer associations, and all interested parties. What changes in practice? Several fundamental aspects.

item.title: Federal Council launches agricultural consultation 2030

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal Council launches consultation on agricultural policy 2030+ (PA30+) - Budget allocated: CHF 13.808 billion for 2030-2033 - Consultation open until December 8, 2026 - 4 areas: margin of maneuver, markets, production bases, sustainability of the chain
## Key facts - **What**: Consultation on agricultural policy 2030+ to increase food security - When: September 2, 2026 – December 8, 2026 (consultation deadline) - Where: Switzerland (federal consultation with cantons, associations, citizens) - Who: Federal Council - Amount: CHF 13.808 billion for 2030-2033 - Implementation: Starting from 2030 - Objective: To increase food security, expand farmers' margin of maneuver, strengthen value creation
### Federal press release of September 2, 2026
Berne, September 2, 2026 — The Federal Council has officially launched the consultation on agricultural policy starting from 2030, named PA30+, with the declared objective of strengthening Switzerland's food security. The consultation remains open until December 8, 2026 and welcomes contributions from farmers, sector organizations, cantonal administrations, and citizens.
With this structural reform, the federal executive intends to expand the entrepreneurial margin of maneuver for Swiss farmers, strengthen added value creation and the efficiency of natural resources. At the same time, the government assigns greater responsibilities to the entire agri-food chain — from the food processing sectors, retail trade, to consumers — to ensure an ecologically, economically, and socially sustainable food system.
### Financial dimension of PA30+
The Federal Council has proposed to Parliament the spending limits for agriculture for the years 2030–2033 amounting to CHF 13.808 billion. This amount is lower by CHF 123 million compared to the financial allocation provided for the years 2026–2029, but exceeds by CHF 80 million the amount that would be maintained by keeping the 2030 financial plan in nominal terms. Parliament will still have to approve these spending limits in the next phase.
### The four strategic areas of PA30+
The Federal Council proposes specific measures articulated on four strategic axes. First, to expand the margin of maneuver and reduce administrative expenditure: currently, direct payments for ecology and animal welfare are strictly tied to the respect of specific prescriptions. PA30+ aims to reorient them towards the achievement of concrete results, giving farmers greater managerial freedom. The digitization of the entire chain will further reduce the administrative burden through a new legal basis that ensures simple and secure data exchange. ### How PA30+ transforms the relationship between farmers, markets, and consumers
The reform introduces a paradigm shift that involves all levels of the Swiss food chain, from agricultural enterprises to the consumer's table.
### Supporting markets and improving economic position
The second area of PA30+ aims to strengthen market observation and extend solidarity measures among operators to support agricultural enterprises in the valorization of their products. Additional financial support is explicitly provided for the dairy and vegetable crops sectors intended for direct human consumption. These measures directly contribute to improving the economic situation of farmers and strengthening their contractual position vis-à-vis distributors.
For those in the agricultural and food processing sectors, this means less market price volatility and better negotiation capacity with large distributors. For Swiss consumers, it translates into greater availability of quality local products, with direct implications for the national [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living).
### Investment in production bases and sustainable technologies
The third strategic axis addresses the structural foundations of Swiss food security: crop protection, promotion of beneficial insects and organisms, support for sustainable technologies, training, and specialized technical advice. These measures also support agricultural enterprises in adapting to climate change, a factor increasingly critical for the stability of Swiss food production.
Compared to the previous phase (2026-2029), the emphasis on resource efficiency and innovative technologies represents an important qualitative leap. It is no longer just about regulatory compliance but a structural modernization strategy for the Swiss primary sector, as desired by the Federal Council.
### Involvement of the supply chain and collective responsibility
The fourth area promotes sustainability throughout the agro-food value chain. Agreements on objectives between the Federal Council and the retail trade are planned, accompanied by initiatives to raise consumer awareness of a balanced diet based on quality Swiss products. PA30+ recognizes that food security is not the sole responsibility of farmers but must be shared by the entire supply chain, from processing to trade, to final consumers. For those working in the Swiss agro-food sector, consult the [job opportunities](nav:jobs) in the food sector.

The public consultation on PA30+ remains open until December 8, 2026. Interested parties — agricultural associations, food industry organizations, trade unions, cantonal administrations, municipalities, environmental organizations, and individual citizens — can submit their contributions to the Federal Council.
Contributions must reach the federal administration by the deadline of December 8, 2026. No specific format is required; however, contributions must clearly state the position of the submitter and the reasons supporting it. The received observations will be analyzed by the Federal Council for possible adjustments before the final presentation to the Federal Parliament.
### Deadlines and next steps
**December 8, 2026**: Final deadline for submitting contributions to the public consultation on PA30+.
After the consultation phase closes, the Federal Council will examine the feedback received from farmers, cantons, industry organizations, and citizens, preparing a revised version of the complete package of measures accompanied by a summary of the consultation results. This version will then be transmitted to Parliament for final approval. The exact timeline for the parliamentary discussion has not yet been set in the federal announcement; however, the operational implementation of PA30+ is scheduled to begin in 2030.
### What to expect in the coming months
Until December, Swiss agricultural associations, food industry organizations, and public and private stakeholders will analyze the PA30+ project in detail. Agricultural businesses will have the opportunity to assess the concrete impact of the new margin of maneuver on their operational management and administrative flows. Consumers will better understand the expected role of PA30+ in the Swiss food system and the collective responsibilities required.
Once the consultation closes on December 8, the Federal Council will transmit the complete dossier to Parliament for approval and possible parliamentary discussion. Swiss farmers, food industry workers, and consumers will thus be involved in one of the most important federal decision-making processes for national food security in the 2030-2040 decade.

item.title: AVS and complementary services in the canton of Aargau
item.description: First pillar of Swiss social security: AHV pension, calculation on contributory history, contributory gaps and supplementary benefits for minimum subsistence.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The AVS pension is the first pillar of Swiss social security - Contribution gaps reduce the amount of the annuity - Complementary benefits fill the gap between annuity and minimum subsistence
## Key facts - **What**: AVS System (Old Age and Survivors Insurance) - Who: UFAS/BSV oversees social security in Switzerland - When: Contributions paid throughout the working career - Where: Each canton (including Aargau) has a compensation fund - Amount: Income calculated on contribution history; supplementary benefits supplement
The first pillar of Swiss social security, managed by the UFAS/BSV (Federal Office of Social Insurance), is based on a mechanism of contributions paid during the entire working career. Each canton, including the canton of Aargau, has a cantonal compensation fund that administers these contributions and determines the amount of the AVS pension.
### How the AVS annuity is calculated
The AVS pension is not fixed: it depends directly on the number of years of contribution paid to the system. Each working year contributes to the final calculation of the service. Those who have paid contributions for their entire career receive the maximum amount; those who have contribution gaps receive a reduced income.
Contribution gaps may result from: - Unemployment periods not covered - Years in which the contribution has not been paid for administrative reasons - Move between cantons without ### Calculation of the pension and effects of gaps
The procedure for calculating the AVS pension follows a uniform national scheme, although it is administered at the cantonal level. The UFAS/BSV defines the parameters; the cantonal compensation fund of Aargau (like any other) applies the formulas to individual cases. To obtain an approximate simulation, you can use the [pension calculator](nav:calculator) available online.
A full year of contributions paid corresponds to one year of contribution. Are there missing contributions? Each missing year proportionally reduces the final pension. Someone who has paid 42 years of contributions out of 45 years of working life will have a reduction in the final pension.
There are mechanisms for filling gaps: it is possible to voluntarily pay back contributions, but within certain deadlines and limits set by law. Not all missing years can be recovered; the system provides well-defined deadlines.
### Supplementary benefits and minimum living standard
Supplementary benefits come into play when the combination of: - AVS pension - Income from other sources (possibly) - Movable/immovable assets
does not reach the minimum threshold set by cantonal law (with federal guidelines). The cantonal compensation fund processes the application and verifies the right.
The amount of the supplementary benefit is the difference between the recognized minimum living standard and the AVS pension received. It is not a fixed contribution but calculated case by case based on the economic situation.
### Difference between supplementary benefits and other subsidies
Do not confuse supplementary benefits (PC) with municipal social assistance, which is a different tool for protecting low incomes. PC are specifically linked to old age and insufficient AVS survivors; social assistance is generic and available for other population groups.
The cantonal compensation fund provides advice on this distinction during the processing of a PC application.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to verify your contribution history
The first step is to request an extract of your contribution history from the cantonal compensation fund of the canton of Aargau (or the canton of your current residence, if you have moved). This extract indicates: - Number of years of contributions paid - Recognized gap years - Amount of pension calculated at the time of request
You can obtain the extract by visiting in person, by mail, or through the online portal of the fund (where available). Many funds offer digital services to view your personal file in real-time.
### Procedure to request supplementary benefits
If the extract shows a low pension or if you know that you will live on an insufficient pension, you can apply for supplementary benefits:
1. Gather documents: copy of the AVS pension decision, income statement, bank statement, real estate ownership certificate (if owner).
2. Fill out the PC application form provided by the cantonal compensation fund.
3. Submit the application to the fund (by mail, email, or counter).
4. Wait for the review; the fund will assess the need according to the established legal criteria.
### Terms and deadlines
Supplementary benefits start from the month following the submission of the application (not retroactive, except for specific exceptions). It is advisable to submit the application before retirement or immediately after receiving the AVS pension decision, to avoid losing months of coverage.
The cantonal compensation fund remains available for telephone consultation, by email, or through a physical counter. Official websites and helplines provide updated information on forms and deadlines.

## Key facts - **What**: Short-term residence permit L - When: Maximum validity up to 12 months - Where: Canton of Aargau - Who: Cantonal migration authorities - Amount: Not specified
The short-term L permit represents a specific category of authorization for foreigners who intend to stay and work in the Swiss territory for a limited period. In the Canton of Aargau, as in the rest of the Confederation, this document is regulated by the provisions of the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration). The validity of this permit is strictly linked to the duration of the employment contract or the specific purpose of the stay. In general, the L permit is issued for a maximum duration of one year, provided that the applicant has a valid employment relationship or sufficient resources for their maintenance.
### Management of validity and extensions The administrative management of residence titles is the responsibility of the cantonal authorities, which evaluate each application based on the current federal legislation. As for the Canton of Aargau, it is necessary to understand that the extension of an L permit is not an automatic act. If the employment relationship should extend beyond the initial expiry date, the employer and the worker must submit a formal renewal request to the competent authorities. This procedure requires proof of the continuity of the employment relationship and compliance with the salary and social conditions in force in the relevant sector. It is essential to emphasize that failure to comply with deadlines or a substantial change in contractual conditions can result in the denial of the extension. The authorities carefully examine the provided documentation to verify that the stay still meets the initial requirements set by the federal law on foreigners and their integration. The practical analysis of the short-term L permit in the Canton of Aargau requires an understanding of the dynamics between federal law and cantonal directives. Unlike B residence permits, which offer greater stability and are generally renewable for longer periods, the L permit is designed for temporary situations. Holders of an L permit must be aware that their status is strictly tied to their employer. This means that in the event of a termination of the employment relationship, the validity of the permit may be reassessed. At the national level, the Swiss system does not provide for a federal minimum wage, however, in sectors where collective labor agreements (CLA) or standard employment contracts (SEC) are present, wage conditions must be guaranteed even for temporary permit holders.

A Swiss court has ordered the promoters of the initiative on neutrality to correct their bulletin. The decision comes after a legal appeal filed by the Greens against the publication of the official communication of the initiative.
Greta Gysin, commenting on the ruling, described the decision as "a clear and important signal." Her statement underscores the significance of the ruling in the context of the campaign for the Swiss neutrality initiative.
### Judicial oversight of democratic communication
The Greens had taken legal action to challenge the publication of the promoters' bulletin. Although the specific details regarding the content of the bulletin and the precise reasons for the objection are not fully specified in the public decision, it is clear that the court deemed a correction in the publication necessary.
This ruling represents a significant judicial intervention in the context of Swiss popular initiatives. It sets a precedent whereby courts can intervene to ensure that the official communications of an initiative meet certain standards of correctness. Maintaining high standards of communication is crucial to preserving the integrity of the Swiss democratic process and ensuring that citizens receive reliable information when called upon to sign or vote on an initiative. ## Popular initiatives in the Swiss democratic system
Popular initiatives are a fundamental tool of Swiss direct democracy. They allow citizens to propose amendments to the federal constitution by collecting a certain number of valid signatures within a set deadline. Once the quorum is reached, the proposal is put to a national popular vote.
Communication during the signature collection phase is therefore crucial: citizens must receive accurate and correct information to make informed decisions when signing the bulletin and, subsequently, when voting on the proposal. The bulletin is the official document that promoters use to collect signatures and contains the text of the proposal, details on the procedure, and the necessary information for citizens to understand what they are supporting.
### The importance of transparency in communication
The ruling that orders promoters to correct their bulletin sets an important precedent: courts can intervene to ensure that the official communications of an initiative meet standards of correctness. This control is not just a matter of form: transparency and accuracy in communication are essential elements to preserve the integrity of the Swiss democratic process.
When the Greens legally appealed, they defended the principle that citizens have the right to receive verified and correct information before making decisions that affect their country. The court's decision to uphold their appeal recognizes this fundamental right. Any inaccuracy in the bulletin could be subject to legal appeal, as demonstrated by the case of the initiative on neutrality. For citizens, it represents an additional protection: the Swiss judicial system can ensure that communications are correct and transparent. For democratic institutions, it reminds us that mutual control among different actors — promoters, media, courts, civil society organizations — is essential for the proper functioning of direct democracy.

item.title: Teacher Shortage: A Report Analyzes Causes and Databases
item.description: The Federal Council approved the report on data collection and assessments concerning teacher shortages.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Federal Council approves report on teacher shortage - Report based on UST data up to 2034 - Multiple causes and regional differences - School reforms do not increase fluctuation
## Key facts - **What**: Report on data collection and evaluations concerning the teacher shortage - When: September 2, 2026 - Where: Bern - Who: Federal Council - Amount: Not specified
The Federal Council approved on September 2, 2026, the report on data collection and evaluations concerning the teacher shortage. The report shows that the phenomenon is due to several factors and that today there is already a solid data base for monitoring and for the measures to be taken, the competence for which lies with the Cantons. The report was drawn up in fulfillment of the postulates 22.4265 and 22.4266 of the Commission for Science, Education and Culture of the National Council (CSEC-N), with which it was requested to shed light on the causes of the teacher shortage and the reasons that lead to staying in or leaving the profession. The report was also to evaluate the school reforms carried out at the national level and the consequences in terms of additional burdens for teachers in a complete and systematic manner.
### Data and analysis The report is based on the statistical data of the Federal Statistical Office (UST) and, more precisely, on the statistics on school personnel, longitudinal analyses and scenarios on the need for teachers up to 2034. In addition, scientific studies and contributions from the Conference of Cantonal Directors of Public Education (CDPE) were also consulted. The teacher shortage is due to various causes, such as demographic trends, the peculiarities of the profession, specific factors related to the school environment, personal situation and needs related to a particular phase of life: these are the conclusions of the Federal Council's report. Statistical analyses generally show both a high stability of the profession and the fact that teachers often do not leave definitively, but rejoin the teaching staff at a later time.
According to the UST scenarios updated for the period 2025-2034, the need for teachers should change in the medium term. The decline in births will result in a lower number of entries into primary school from around 2027, and thus a lower need for new teachers. However, regional differences remain, which require foresight from the Cantons in school and personnel planning. ### Practical implications For the evaluation of school reforms, given the federal distribution of competencies, there can be neither national school reforms promoted by the Confederation nor federal evaluations of these reforms for the entire Switzerland. Reforms are coordinated and possibly evaluated at the cantonal or linguistic region level. The consulted research also shows that reforms alone do not lead to greater teacher fluctuation: for teachers, an additional burden is created, especially when new requirements do not provide adequate support or sufficient explanations regarding skills.
The report concludes that, at the national level, there is already a solid data base for monitoring teacher shortages and for the adoption of cantonal measures. Personal reasons for resignations and perceived overload only emerge to a limited extent from administrative data. Collecting this type of information is primarily the responsibility of the cantons. The Confederation plays a supportive role, particularly in providing reliable data and exchanging knowledge and best practices.
### Comparison with the previous situation Before the approval of this report, the cantons had difficulty planning school personnel due to the lack of reliable data and a long-term vision. With the availability of this new data, the cantons will be able to adopt more targeted and effective measures to address teacher shortages. This improvement in planning could lead to greater stability in school personnel and better quality of education.

This could include training new teachers, offering incentives to stay in the profession, and creating a more supportive work environment. The Confederation will continue to support the Cantons by providing reliable data and promoting the exchange of good practices.
